[[No overall control]]{{efn|Liberal Democrats minority}} | after_election = TBD | after_party = [[No overall control]] }} The '''2026 Three Rivers District Council election''' was held on 7 May 2026, alongside the [[2026 United Kingdom local elections|other local elections across the United Kingdom]] being held on the same day, to elect 13 of 39 members of [[Three Rivers District Council]] in [[Hertfordshire]], England.{{Cite web|title=Council wants Three Rivers elections to go ahead as planned|url=https://www.threerivers.gov.uk/news/three-rivers-elections--may-2026|website=www.threerivers.gov.uk|access-date=2026-01-30|language=en}} ==Summary== ===Background=== In [[2024 Three Rivers District Council election|2024]], the [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] retained control of the council.{{Cite news|title=Three Rivers result - Local Elections 2024|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/election/2024/england/councils/E07000102|work=BBC News|access-date=2026-01-30|language=en-GB}}{{Cite web|title=District Council Election Results 2 May 2024|url=https://www.threerivers.gov.uk/services/elections-and-democracy/election-results/district-council-election-results-may-2024|website=www.threerivers.gov.uk|access-date=2026-01-30|language=en}} However, the council was in [[no overall control]] after the Conservatives subsequently won two by-elections in the previously safe Liberal Democrat ward of Abbots Langley and Bedmond.
